environment.description: Process runs under a pivot_root(2) confinement established by the container runtime (runc) with a custom OCI bundle spec. The rootfs is a minimal scratch image containing only the Go binary and /var/spool/processed/ as a tmpfs. The /etc/secrets/ path is bind-mounted as a FIFO-backed fuse-secrets-store-csi-driver volume that serves the key exactly once during process initialization and then returns EACCES on subsequent reads. The spool directory is a tmpfs with a 64KB size limit and noexec. Critically, the Kafka connection uses mutual TLS with a short-lived certificate (5 min TTL) issued by a Vault PKI backend, and the Kafka cluster ACL restricts this consumer's group to READ-only on the single partition with no ability to produce or consume from other topics. The pod runs with a seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault augmented with a custom SECCOMP_FILTER) that blocks ptrace, process_vm_readv, and /proc/*/mem access. Network egress is restricted via Cilium L7 policy to only the Kafka broker endpoints on port 9093 (TLS). The combination means: (1) an attacker cannot read the key file after init, (2) cannot exfiltrate spool contents over network, (3) the tmpfs size limit means only ~4 messages can be spooled before writes fail, and (4) the mTLS + Kafka ACL prevents an attacker from injecting chosen plaintexts or reading other consumers' traffic to perform the nonce-reuse attack.

config.network_policy: Cilium L7: egress only to kafka-broker-{1,2}:9093
config.kafka_auth: mTLS with Vault PKI (5min cert TTL)
config.kafka_acl: READ on payment-events partition 0 only, no WRITE, no DESCRIBE on other topics
